speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. Can you describe the severity and duration of the bleeding following your wisdom tooth extraction, and have you noticed any other unusual bleeding or bruising episodes in the past?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you experience frequent nosebleeds or prolonged bleeding from minor cuts? Have you ever noticed blood in your urine or stool?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling. A doctor I saw earlier said this was very likely Gastroenteritis and told me the presentation was already quite typical.

speaker: Doctor
text: The previous diagnosis of gastroenteritis is incorrect given the bleeding history. Given the family history of joint swelling (hemarthrosis) and easy bruising, I suspect a factor deficiency like Hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: aPTT and PT

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Partial Thromboplastin Time: 60 sec, Prothrombin Time: 15 sec

speaker: Doctor
text: The prolonged aPTT with a normal PT, combined with your family history of joint swelling, strongly suggests Hemophilia. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII and Factor IX levels

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Factor VIII level: 5%, Factor IX level: 100%

speaker: Doctor
text: Your Factor VIII level is critically low at 5%, while Factor IX is normal, which confirms a diagnosis of Hemophilia A. DIAGNOSIS READY: Hemophilia A
